entries.summary: When the user asks for a one-off script, prefer single-file output unless an explicit project structure is requested.
entries.body: Single-file scripts have lower setup friction and are easier to copy/share. Reach for a multi-file structure only when the user names a framework or asks for a project scaffold.

entries.summary: In TypeScript, prefer explicit return types on exported functions; inferred types are fine for locals.
Before creating a new utility, search the codebase for an existing helper that already solves the same problem.
